articles.title: Embattled Nvidia CEO reportedly involved in a 2nd extramarital affair
articles.summary: Nvidia ( NVDA ) stock tanked in after-hours trading following a report from the New York Times that embattled Nvidia ( NVDA ) CEO Jensen Huang was allegedly involved in a second extramarital affair. The company's board is reportedly meeting to determine if it will oust Huang as chief executive, the Wall Street Journal reports . According to the report, Huang, whose relationship with a woman alleged to be a Chinese spy has embroiled the company in scandal this week, also had a relationship with Nvidia executive Kimberly Powell. Nvidia stock fell in after-hours trading following the report. The Times report says that Huang and Powell were seen being affectionate at a hotel during a company conference in March. Huang is already under investigation for an affair with Alice Huang, an alleged Chinese spy. The CEO admitted the affair in a memo to employees. "I was unfaithful to my wife. My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry," Huang wrote. The Information reported on Tuesday that Alice Huang is believed to be involved in a network of Chinese companies that facilitated the shipment of $7.5 billion ‌in chip sales to China. Given the size and importance of Nvidia in the stock market today, the revelation marks one of the biggest CEO-personal conduct scandals in history . It also highlights Nvidia's key-person risk and uncertain succession plan as questions swirl about whether the board will ask Huang to step down. The news has drawn immediate and varied reactions from leaders ranging from the US president to other CEOs. President Trump stood by Huang, calling him "an honorable guy," but other members of the president's party are expected to put more scrutiny on the company. Trump also stated on Monday that the FBI was looking into Huang's relationship. In a statement on Sunday, Nvidia's board said it has "no reason to believe that either national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised." Follow along for live updates and reactions. articles.title: Democrat Scott Colom flips Mississippi Senate seat in a historic upset
articles.summary: Mississippi Democrat Scott Colom has narrowly defeated Republican Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith to flip another Senate seat for Democrats. According to figures from the Associated Press, Colom won 49.2% of the vote in the closely contested race, which was called more than a week after Election Day. Hyde-Smith finished with 48.7%. Mississippi — one of the reddest states in the country — wasn't really on the national radar prior to the elections. However, early results showed the two candidates separated by as few as 43 votes, indicating a shock was brewing. The outcome expands Democrats' total number of Senate seats to 55, following a midterms rout that has seen the GOP lose control of the U.S. Senate and U.S. House. Colom becomes the first elected Black U.S. senator from Mississippi in more than 140 years and the state’s first Democratic senator since 1989. Prior to the result being declared, Colom had repeatedly expressed confidence that his campaign would prevail, flooding the airwaves and attending at least eight events. "It's very clear the direction of this," he told reporters on Friday . Hyde-Smith delivered a concession message in a video posted on X Wednesday evening : “While this is not the outcome we worked for or hoped for, I respect the decision of Mississippi voters,” she said. “I want to congratulate Scott Colom and wish him well as he takes on the tremendous responsibility of representing our great state.” Alaska is now the only remaining Senate race to be called. Democrat Mary Peltola holds the lead on 49%, with 84% of the vote counted. Republican incumbent Sen. Dan Sullivan is on 47.2%, according to the latest AP figures. Who is Scott Colom? Colom, 43, was born in Columbus, Miss., to two lawyers who also participated in politics. In 1987, his father, Wilbur, ran for state treasurer as a Republican; his mother, Dorothy, served as the first Black Chancery Court judge in their home district. Colom earned his JD from the University of Wisconsin in 2009 and went on to serve as the first Black justice court judge in Lowndes County, Miss., before becoming the first Black city prosecutor in Columbus. In 2015, Colom defeated a nearly 30-year incumbent to become the first Black district attorney elected in a majority-white voting district in Mississippi history. He has since prosecuted a number of high-profile murder and sexual assault cases. Colom gives an update about his Senate race on Nov. 4, 2026 in Jackson, Miss. Rogelio V. Solis/Getty Images In 2022, President Joe Biden nominated Colom to serve as federal judge for the Northern District of Mississippi. Leading Magnolia State Republicans — including Sen. Roger Wicker and former Govs. Phil Bryant and Haley Barbour — backed Colom's nomination. "I have known two generations of the Colom family for over 20 years and believe Scott Colom possesses the discernment to be a fair and exemplary judge," Bryant told the New York Times . But Hyde-Smith blocked Colom's nomination in the Senate, citing support his 2015 campaign received from a political action committee funded by George Soros and claiming that he favored allowing transgender athletes to compete in girls' and women's sports. The White House characterized Hyde-Smith's concerns as " spurious ." In a letter to Hyde-Smith urging her to reconsider, Colom confirmed that he had signed a letter with other prosecutors condemning efforts to criminalize gender-affirming care for transgender people, but insisted that their joint statement "did not comment on legislation specifically related to participation in athletics." Colom also said he had not known about Soros's contributions to the Mississippi Safety and Justice PAC "until I read about them in my hometown paper." Colom's unsuccessful nomination was returned to Biden on Jan. 3, 2024. In September 2025, Colom announced his U.S. Senate candidacy. How Colom caught up Hyde-Smith, 67, is a former lobbyist and state legislator who was serving as Mississippi's agriculture and commerce commissioner when she was appointed to the U.S. Senate in 2018 following the resignation of Republican Sen. Thad Cochran. She won a 2018 special election and a 2020 full-term election, and she has served in the Senate ever since. There were signs before Election Day that Hyde-Smith might be vulnerable to "voter apathy," as one Mississippi State University political science professor recently put it . Sen. Wicker won reelection in 2024 by 25 points; Hyde-Smith's margin of victory in 2020 was less than half that. And while the only polls made public this cycle showed Hyde-Smith ahead , her leads were stuck in the single digits — no survey put her support above 50%. One April Democratic poll showed Hyde-Smith trailing a hypothetical "someone else" 33% to 53%. Hyde-Smith speaks at a campaign event in Corinth, Miss., on Oct. 26, 2026. Madison Thorn/Bloomberg via Getty Images Regardless, Hyde-Smith seemed content to coast to reelection, barely bothering to appear on the campaign trail. But Colom didn't have that luxury — and when he cut a viral campaign ad about beef prices in mid-October, the tide started to turn. Asked earlier this year about soaring costs, including the price of beef, Hyde-Smith told local TV station WLOX that "all commodities go through peaks and valleys," but "you have so many proteins to choose from." In the final weeks of the campaign, Colom seized on Hyde-Smith's remark about "proteins" to mock her with a spot featuring incredulous Mississippians grilling burgers, dining out and shopping for groceries — and saying they'd rather "pick another senator instead" (along with other, more colorful language). The video has since racked up nearly 19 million views on Colom's X account . She done lost her damn mind. pic.twitter.com/wHPt4PSAob — Scott Colom (@scott_colom) October 13, 2026 When the ad took off, national Democrats sprang into action. The Senate Majority PAC poured $2.2 million into the race; Senate Democrats' campaign arm contributed another $500,000. Former President Barack Obama filmed an endorsement ad. Former President Bill Clinton, former Vice President Kamala Harris and Sens. Cory Booker of New Jersey and Raphael Warnock of Georgia rushed to Mississippi to rally with Colom. In response, Republicans were forced to play defense, sending Trump to Mississippi in the final days of the campaign (along with cash infusions of their own). In the end, it wasn't enough to secure Hyde-Smith victory. When Trump came to Mississippi, Colom went to his event to talk to rally-goers about health care, grocery bills and gas prices. "I got the best message ever for Republican voters in Mississippi," he told CNN afterward. "I'm going to get you what you were promised in 2024. You were promised lower grocery prices on Day One. That's what I will fight for. You were promised no more endless wars. That's what I will fight for. You were promised the full and transparent release of the Epstein files. That's what I will fight for." articles.title: Brooklyn building collapse leaves at least 1 person dead; rescue operations underway
articles.summary: At least one person is dead and multiple others injured, including an individual who is trapped, after a building collapsed in Brooklyn, according to New York City authorities. The FDNY said rescue operations are underway after responding to reports of people trapped following a building collapse in the Flatbush neighborhood. Angelina Katsanis/Reuters - PHOTO: Emergency personnel work at the scene of a partial building collapse where, according to local reports, people are trapped in Brooklyn, Nov. 11, 2026. A three-story building collapsed into an open excavation site, where workers were on scene, according to an FDNY dispatch. The wall of another three-story building that now stands next to the site was also shorn off, exposing apartments. One person was pronounced dead at the scene, according to the New York Police Department. Ten people were injured, including two critically, according to the FDNY. The injured include one person who remains trapped, the department said. Earlier, the FDNY said several construction workers were being transported to the hospital for treatment, and firefighters were trying to get a count of all the workers on the job site. The site under construction is being developed into a nine-story, mixed-use building, with plans for a grocery store and medical center on the ground floor and apartments on the upper floors, permit records show. Angelina Katsanis/Reuters - PHOTO: Emergency personnel work at the scene of a partial building collapse in Brooklyn, Nov. 11, 2026. Michael M. Santiago/Getty Images - PHOTO: Members of the FDNY respond to the scene of a partial building collapse, Nov. 11, 2026, in Brooklyn. The first 911 call came in at 4:01 p.m., according to the FDNY. Firefighters could be seen in debris in a construction pit in the area of Flatbush and Bedford Avenues. Amid the massive response, at least two people could be seen being rescued from the rubble, pulled out on stretchers. WABC - PHOTO: Firefighters carry a person on a stretcher after they were pulled out of a collapsed building in Brooklyn, Nov. 11, 2026. The NYC Department of Buildings said its inspectors "are on scene at a major building collapse near Flatbush Avenue in Brooklyn assisting with recovery operations and conducting structural stability inspections of nearby buildings." NYC Council Member Farah Louis, who represents Flatbush, called the images from the site "heartbreaking." Ryan Murphy/AP  - PHOTO: First responders work the scene after a building collapsed in the Brooklyn borough of New York, Nov. 11, 2026. "We are devastated to learn that at least one life has been lost, with multiple people reported trapped and several injured as emergency personnel work urgently to reach everyone in the rubble," Louis said in a statement. "My immediate priority is the safety of everyone impacted, and my team is actively working to reach affected families to connect them with critical information and support during this frightening time," the statement continued. New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani urged people to avoid the area amid the rescue response. "As emergency operations continue, please join me in holding our neighbors and the members of this community in our hearts," he said in a statement. This is a developing story. Please check back for updates. This article originally appeared on ABC News at https://abcnews.com/US/rescue-operations-underway-after-building-collapses-brooklyn-new/story?id=138059620

articles.title: Democrats frustrated by absences in failed Hegseth impeachment vote
articles.summary: From left: Nancy Pelosi, Steven Horsford and Haley Stevens missed the vote on Tuesday evening. Composite: Getty Images, Bloomberg Democratic lawmakers expressed outrage at nearly a dozen of their colleagues for missing a vote Tuesday evening to impeach the defense secretary, Pete Hegseth , allowing Republicans to defeat the effort. Eleven Democrats missed the key procedural vote on the impeachment effort , which failed by just seven votes. Some blamed traffic and conflicting events and others accused Speaker Mike Johnson of closing the vote early. Many of those not in the Capitol said they support the effort to impeach Hegseth. “You should show up and do your job,” Abdul El-Sayed , the senator-elect of Michigan, said on CNN to the Democratic lawmakers Tuesday. Richard Ojeda, the representative-elect of North Carolina, told CNN that the Democratic representatives “failed” by not voting. “Shame on them for not showing up,” Ojeda said on Tuesday. “I mean, this is important … they had an opportunity to finally get rid of this buffoonery we had.” The missing Democrats gave House Republicans the numbers to shelve the impeachment effort by voting 211 – 204 to refer eight articles of impeachment against Hegseth to a House committee. Speaking at Arlington national cemetery to mark Veterans Day, Donald Trump praised Hegseth and said he had done a “fantastic job” as the Pentagon head. “I had a feeling that was going to happen,” the president said of the failed effort to impeach Hegseth, adding: “He loves you, and he protects you – he’s all about you.” The articles, introduced by Republican Thomas Massie , included charges of violating congressional authority by waging war in Iran . The effort came after voters overwhelming cast ballots for Democratic candidates in the 2026 midterms, largely in rebuke of the Trump administration’s policies – including the war in Iran. Sydney Kamlager-Dove, a representative from California, told MeidasTouch there was “no reason why we should have lost this vote because of attendance issues”. “This is what the people have been talking about … so shame on folks who were not here because these people lost,” Kamlager-Dove added. Melanie Stansbury of New Mexico wrote on X that she was “blocked from entering the Capitol to vote due to a traffic incident and a police escort of a bus during the vote”. “When she reached the chamber the vote had just gaveled out. She immediately filed a report of her vote of ‘NO’ to the motion meant to kill the impeachment articles and refer them to the Judiciary Committee, as documented in the Congressional Record,” Stansbury wrote, adding that Hegseth “must be impeached now”. Laura Gillen of New York similarly wrote on X she too was stuck in traffic but “strongly” believes Hegseth should be impeached. Jonathan Jackson, of Illinois, wrote on X that he also was stuck behind the traffic jam. Brittany Pettersen of Colorado wrote on X that she was “denied” the ability to vote. Member of Pettersen’s office later told 9News she too was stuck in traffic. Julia Brownley of California wrote on Facebook that Johnson “closed the vote” before she could make it to the House floor. “As I and many of my colleagues were rushing to the floor to support Hegseth’s impeachment, Mike Johnson closed the vote before we could,” Brownley wrote. Marilyn Strickland of Washington also missed the vote by one minute because she was stuck behind a motocade, but that she would have voted to impeach Hegseth, Strickland’s office told Politico . Nancy Pelosi of California missed the vote because she was in San Francisco to meet with local veterans and accept a Lifetime Advocate for Veterans Award, Pelosi’s spokesperson told SFGate . Lou Correa of California wrote on Instagram that he was undergoing a medical procedure and remaining in his district until he was medically cleared. Steven Horsford of Nevada, Haley Stevens of Michigan and Frederica Wilson of Florida did not provide public reasons for their absence on Tuesday. Several Democratic lawmakers who did vote on the effort to impeach Hegseth noted that they were also busy with other life events but still made their way to the Capitol. Pat Ryan of New York wrote on X that he was recovering from back surgery but left the hospital early in order to cast his vote. Congressman Glenn Ivey, a Maryland Democrat, called the absence of the 11 lawmakers during Tuesday’s vote “certainly disappointing”, but said there would be “other chances” to advance impeachment efforts. In an interview, Ivey said he was “absolutely” supportive of renewing the push when Democrats regain control of both chambers in January. At the same time, he argued that voters made clear that concerns about the cost of living remain their top priority. “There aren’t a lot of people, in my district anyway, [whose ability] to stay in their house depends on whether Hegseth gets impeached or not,” Ivey said. “We’ve been calling it the affordability agenda, but I think for many people, it’s really a survivability agenda, and we need to be focused on that.” • This story was updated on 11 November 2026. A previous version incorrectly stated that Brittany Pettersen is a lawmaker from California; she is from Colorado. articles.title: Ole Miss students speak out after viral video of alleged racist taunts
articles.summary: The Black college students who were harassed by two White students at the University of Mississippi making monkey gestures and sounds outside their apartment are speaking out after the incident went viral. The women said they were familiar with the stories of racism some faced at Ole Miss over the years — the school didn't allow its first Black student, James Meredith, until 1962, for instance — but they were not prepared for what they experienced last Friday. Jakirya Metcalf, a freshman at Ole Miss, said she was in her apartment last Friday night when she saw the video on her Ring camera . "We actually went outside and tried to, like, approach them and get them to explain why they did that," Metcalf told "CBS Mornings." "One girl was like, 'I'm sorry we did that to four doors,'" Victoria Johnson, one of the roommates, said. "And mind you, we didn't see any one of those doors. It was just ours that was targeted. And she was like, 'We didn't mean any harm.'" Metcalf and Johnson said the first person seen on the video, Aliana Kunes, apologized. But the second person, who made monkey sounds toward the camera, doubled down off-camera. "She continued to make the gestures after the girl was apologizing," Johnson said. "It was like a slap in the face." "I had said that I don't think they should go around because even if they go to other people's door and do that, I don't think they should do that because it's very disrespectful," Metcalf said. Kunes apologized for her actions in a statement Tuesday. "To the women I offended and to the Ole Miss community, I sincerely apologize," she wrote. "Before the incident on November 6, I never met the women involved and was unaware of their race, however, I recognize my actions were insensitive, inappropriate, and deeply harmful. I would have never intentionally made those noises or gestures toward a person of color. I have apologized to the women and I pray they will forgive me." Kunes voluntarily withdrew from the university after issuing the statement Tuesday. When asked if she accepted Kunes' apology, Metcalf said she had mixed feelings. "I feel like no matter like who we are, or if she knew our race or not, but the gestures and the voices, I feel like it still was very disrespectful," she said. "I appreciate the apology, but I feel like it still doesn't change what happened on that Friday, because it's still hurtful and it's still devastating that someone would come to our camera and do that," Kaiyden Caldwell, another of the roommates, told "CBS Mornings." Johnson's mother, Chiquita Laó, said she was surprised to learn Kunes withdrew from the university after Kunes said she was harassed. "I hate to hear that because you know the children are the future, but I feel like everybody needs to be accountable," Laó said. University officials said in a statement they are investigating the incident and have spoken with those targeted. "The university has been and will continue providing care and resources to our students," the school said in a statement on Wednesday. "We have met with the impacted students and their families to offer support and discuss the relevant processes, and the investigation is moving forward. Student privacy laws prohibit the university from commenting on any specific student, including any potential disciplinary action." Metcalf, Caldwell and Johnson said they plan to stay at Ole Miss and said they won't let the incident ruin their time at the school. CBS News reached out to the two other women in the video but did not hear back. "I want people to be mindful of their actions now," Johnson said. "So when people who would potentially experience the same situations to speak out and don't let things be swept under the rug, because this is a reality for us, and I feel like voices need to be heard." articles.title: Hegseth's group reprimanded by guard at Tomb of the Unknown Soldier
articles.summary: WASHINGTON (AP) — A soldier guarding the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier issued a verbal reprimand to a group of advisers and staffers with Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth following a Veterans Day ceremony at Arlington National Cemetery. Video shows Hegseth taking photos on the empty steps in front of the tomb with his wife, Jennifer, chief of staff Ricky Buria, deputy chief of staff Patrick Weaver and senior adviser Tami Radabaugh. As the group broke from taking photos, a loud laugh could be heard, and the soldier guarding the tomb shouted that “all visitors will maintain an atmosphere of silence and respect at all times.” Sean Parnell, the Pentagon’s top spokesman, said that “while commemorating this solemn day, a soldier correctly and respectfully reminded everyone to maintain decorum.” “The Secretary and the entire Department have always honored — and will always honor — the sacrifices our military men and women have made to keep America safe,” he added. The tomb is considered to be one of the most solemn and revered war memorials in the U.S., being the final resting place of unidentified soldiers from World War I, World War II and the Korean War. It has been guarded around the clock — rain or shine — by a soldier from the Army’s 3rd Infantry Regiment, also known as “The Old Guard," since 1948. Hegseth and his staff were at the tomb as part of a larger ceremony commemorating Veterans Day that also was attended by President Donald Trump and Vice President JD Vance. The incident comes a day after Hegseth narrowly survived an effort to impeach him by lawmakers in Congress. The effort was led by Rep. Thomas Massie, R-Ky., and backed by Democrats. However, while Hegseth's critics were not successful in Tuesday's vote, Republicans may have only delayed efforts to impeach the defense secretary. With Democrats set to take control of the House and Senate in January, those efforts are likely to be renewed. Hegseth rebuked the effort Tuesday in his first news conference in months, arguing that he had committed none of the high crimes required in the Constitution for his removal. A core part of his argument included the assertion that criticisms of him and his handling of the U.S. military were tantamount to an indictment against the nation’s service members and their successes. “On the eve of Veterans Day, these resolutions tell every one of them that their service was a crime,” Hegseth said Tuesday. “This is not patriotism,” Hegseth argued. “This is sabotage.” Following the reprimand at Arlington National Cemetery on Wednesday, the reaction from Democrats was swift. Rep. Gwen Moore, D-Wis., said Hegseth demonstrated “his utter lack of fitness for his office.” “One day after narrowly avoiding impeachment, he shows his contempt for our men and women in uniform by disrespecting the sanctity of the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier,” she wrote in a social media post . It was not the first time members of Trump's team have caused controversy at Arlington National Cemetery. During his campaign for a second term, Trump attended a ceremony in 2024 to honor U.S. forces killed in the Iraq and Afghanistan wars. A campaign staffer reportedly shoved a cemetery employee trying to prevent two people from filming and photographing the event. Trump, who had been invited by troops’ families, later shared a video on TikTok showing him at the cemetery with a voiceover blaming the Biden administration for the “disaster” of the Afghanistan withdrawal . U.S. law prohibits campaign or election-related activities within national military cemeteries. articles.title: Joe Biden says he wouldn't have run in 2024 if he'd known he had cancer
articles.summary: NEED TO KNOW Joe Biden gets candid about his stage 4 prostate cancer as he releases his new memoir , Promise Me, America The former president reflects on life, withdrawing from the 2024 race and the legacy he hopes to leave Dr. Jill Biden describes the daily realities of caring for her husband with support from their family Two days after the Democrats swept the midterm elections , former President Joe Biden has that signature twinkle in his blue eyes. “Look at the people we got elected: first women governors, first Black governors,” he tells PEOPLE with a quiet rasp. At 83, and living with stage 4 prostate cancer — for which he completed radiation and is undergoing hormone therapy — Biden is slower than when he suddenly withdrew from the presidential race in 2024 following a disastrous debate against Donald Trump and amid concerns about his health. Still, his perennial optimism remains. “I’m not saying I’ll live forever,” says the one-term president, seated in the dining room of his Wilmington, Del., lake house, “but the point is that I have all my faculties, I have access to all the things I had before and I feel good.” Former President Joe Biden in his study at home in Wilmington, Del., on Nov. 5. Credit: Victoria Will He’s fighting the disease “like hell,” Biden writes in his presidential memoir, Promise Me, America , out Nov. 17. Through it all, his wife, Dr. Jill Biden , 75, has been by his side. Being a family caregiver — like 63 million Americans — is “emotionally, physically hard,” the former first lady says after returning home from volunteering at a women’s prison, where she teaches literature part-time. Although she has help looking after her husband and says family is a constant at the house, “My days are making sure he eats right. Does he exercise? Is he taking the right medicine? Did I talk to the doctor?” Reality came into focus when she read a magazine at a nail salon and imagined traveling to the destinations on the glossy pages. “All of a sudden it struck me, like, ‘Wait a minute, this isn’t our life now,’ ” she says. “We’re on a new journey.” With no questions off the table, President Biden addresses his life and health now, his presidency and the legacy he hopes to leave behind. In May 2025, 118 days after you left office, you announced that you had been diagnosed with stage 4 prostate cancer that had spread to your bones. You write that you’re fighting it with the “help of an incredible medical team and an even better family.” What does that fight look like? It looks very positive. There’s a lot of people who’ve been diagnosed with cancer, particularly the kind of cancer I have, who live long lives, who live for another 10, 20 years. And so far, the two tests that have been done show that the cancer is not metastasized beyond what it already was ... There are eight different pills I take a day. Former President Joe Biden at home in Wilmington, Del., on Nov. 5, 2026 Credit: Victoria Will Next June will mark your 50th wedding anniversary. What has cancer taught you about your marriage that you didn’t know before? Nothing. I knew from the beginning what she was. Jill is, first of all, bright as hell. Secondly, I think she’s the most beautiful woman in the world, which every husband probably thinks, but I believe it. And we have a real partnership. Joe Biden and wife Jill Biden pose for a photo together with their cat in May 2025. Credit: Joe Biden/X How has your family, including your grandchildren and your great-grandchild, supported you? They’re always here. “Can we come up, Pop? Pop, can we do this?” I do more with my grandchildren than I do with anybody else, and that’s for real. I’m interested and they’re interested in serious things as well ... They’re involved in a lot of things having to do with public service. They participate in a number of issues that relate to the well-being of the country. They’re the loves of my life. The Biden family celebrated Easter 2026 in Santa Ynez, California As the second Catholic to become president, you’ve been candid about how your faith has guided you through hard times. Do you still see signs of those you’ve lost? I do. I see signs of their love in their progeny. I see signs of their love of things that I find out that they have done that I didn’t know they had done before ... My son Hunter , he and his brother Beau were born a year and a day apart. They’re each other’s best friends in the world. When Beau died, it was a blow to Hunter in a way that was almost beyond repair ... Now he’s deeply involved in public policy things. He’s deeply involved in making the case, but he’s straight as an arrow in terms of his alcoholism. My dad used to have an expression: “Joey, family’s the beginning, the middle and the end.” And that’s how it is. You write, “People say I was deluding myself that I could do the job [of president] at my age. My answer to that is: I was doing the job.” Why do you think they felt that way? It’s natural. If tomorrow you’re going to say that the head of your [company] is going to be hired on as an 80-year-old person, you go, “What the hell’s going on?” But the value I think I brought was I knew so many of the leaders, I knew their inclinations, I knew what was going on, and many of them came to me. I thought it was value added, not subtracted. Standard medical guidelines don’t recommend routine prostate cancer screenings for men over 70. You write, “I was treated no differently from any other 82-year-old man in America. Maybe I should have been.” What do you say to Americans who believe that a screening should have been part of your annual physical? Look, White House doctors are doing what the whole entire medical profession is doing ... I had some discomfort, and Jill thought, Why isn’t that test done for men who are in their 70s? And there wasn’t any particular [sign] except recurring pain. When he wasn’t downing a black-and-white milkshake, former President Joe Biden chatted with diners at the Charcoal Pit in Wilmington, Del., his favorite diner since high school, on Nov. 5. Credit: Victoria Will You describe a “cynical twist” on your cancer news: that some folks said you hid your cancer as president. Why do you think they reacted that way? A lot of people do that. They hide bad news from the public if they’re elected officials. I didn’t do that. We let the public know when I found out, when I knew what was going on. I think it’s important for a national leader, as president, to let people know they go through some of the very same things that a lot of American people are going through ... I wasn’t hiding it at all. Many have spoken about the toll of the Presidency. How might your undiagnosed cancer have exacerbated that? First of all, I never felt the toll. I read [others] like Harry Truman talk about [how] it’s the most difficult job in the world. I didn’t find it that way. And so I, quite frankly, found that it didn’t in any way interfere with my job. Former President Joe Biden in his study at home in Wilmington, Del., on Nov. 5 Credit: Victoria Will What do you miss the most about the job? The staff, the people in the White House. They’re good people, from the people making sure there’s a sheet on the bed to the people who are taking care of all the visitors that come through. They all have a sense of honor, what they’re doing in the White House. It’s the People’s House. What’s your reaction to the Trump ballroom and the East Wing being destroyed? Almost as disturbing as the gold bars on the walls of the White House and the Oval Office. I mean, what the hell are we talking about? I find it disturbing ... I’ve viewed the president’s judgment in tearing down the East Wing and a number of other things as nothing more than to try to create monuments to himself: “I built that.” I find it beneath the country. After Donald Trump defeated Kamala Harris in 2024, he and Melania returned to the White House on Jan. 20, 2025. Credit: Jim WATSON/AFP/Getty It’s been two years and four months since that debate moment on the stage with Trump. What is your perspective on it now? Look, I don’t know anybody who hasn’t made a mistake in a debate. To me, it was not very consequential. First of all, I thought there’d be another debate, which there wasn’t. But notwithstanding the fact that there wasn’t another debate, it didn’t disturb me because it wasn’t consequential. Former President Joe Biden chatted with staff at the Charcoal Pit, his favorite diner since high school, in Wilmington, Del., on Nov. 5. Credit: Victoria Will In hindsight, looking at the 2024 election, is there anything you would’ve done differently? What I can’t say, because there’s no evidence of it — if I had known that I was feeling lousy because I had cancer, I would have resigned. I would’ve not gone forward, because I don’t think an 80-year-old man with cancer should be running for [president]. But that wasn’t the case ... I believe that on an objective basis, I was the best-equipped person to do the job. Hunter has been speaking out on podcasts and social media. What do you make of that? Hunter is one of the brightest men I know. He has more moral and physical courage than most people I know, and I’m really proud of him. He’s making the case as to how we should proceed as a country. He’s said of the pardon you gave him: “Was it good for our Constitution? Was it good for the American people? Was it good for my father’s legacy? No on all accounts.” What’s your perspective? I disagree ... I watched the modus operandi of Trump. He goes after people without any basis, whether they’re viewed as an enemy. I knew what he would do. If I hadn’t pardoned — not just some of my family members, anyone who’s dealt with me—he would go back and try to do harm to them, as I’ve observed. Never miss a story — sign up for PEOPLE’s free daily newsletter to stay up-to-date on the best of what PEOPLE has to offer, from celebrity news to compelling human interest stories. In your book, for the first time, you share the letter that Trump left you in the Oval Office after you beat him in the 2020 election. Your takeaway: “It was almost as if there were two Donald Trumps.” What do you mean? That could have been written by President Kennedy to me or by President Johnson or by George Bush. I mean, it was gracious, it was generous, and it was totally inconsistent with the kind of president he’d been. Joe Biden’s new book, “Promise Me, America,” out Nov. 17 You write, “Promise me, America, that we will be the nation we know in our hearts we can be and should be.” What does that nation mean to you at 83, after more than 50 years of public service? It means to continue to hold those truths to be self-evident, that we’re all created equal. I got involved in politics because of the Civil Rights movement. It means to be engaged in trying to help make the country a better place than it has been, to give people the benefit of the doubt ... When I say, “Promise me, America,” I mean, America, you know the promises we made. Let’s keep them. Joe Biden was sworn in on his family Bible when he became president on Jan. 20, 2021. Credit: Kent Nishimura/Los Angeles Times/Getty How do you want the American people to remember you? I tell you, it’s the greatest honor any man or woman could be given anywhere to be the President of the United States of America. And I hope I kept the promise of America ... I didn’t say I didn’t make mistakes—but I meant what I said, and I did what I said I was going to do. PEOPLE VIPs can read our full conversation with Joe Biden in this week’s issue, available right now in the app . articles.title: A 67-year-old Democratic veteran is becoming the left's favorite to replace Schumer
articles.summary: Progressive lawmakers and activists are hoping to harness momentum from last week’s sweeping Democratic victories to install inspiring new congressional leaders. Many have looked at the Senate and found their guy: a 67-year-old father of three from an affluent Washington suburb who has held public office continuously since 1991. Sen. Chris Van Hollen of Maryland has emerged as the alternative of choice for a swath of Democrats who believe Chuck Schumer, the longtime Senate Democratic leader, should step aside despite presiding over massive midterm gains. It’s the culmination of a remarkable resurgence for Van Hollen, who spent years inching up the Democratic leadership ladder in the House only to ditch his seniority there for the back benches of the Senate in 2017. Over the past two years, he has emerged as an increasingly strident critic of the Democratic party establishment and its approach to President Donald Trump, as well as its positions on populist economic policies and the U.S. relationship with Israel — and members of the party’s left flank have noticed. A wave of House Democrats, outside activists and even at least one newly elected senator are effectively trying to draft him into what could be an uphill race to unseat the 75-year-old Schumer as majority leader. “I have been very impressed by Senator Van Hollen’s leadership,” said Sen.-elect Peggy Flanagan of Minnesota, who beat a more centrist Democrat in her state’s primary and has said she will not back Schumer. Van Hollen has wavered on whether he is pursuing a role in Senate leadership or perhaps instead a 2028 run for the presidency. He said Tuesday he is “actively listening” as he keeps the door open to a majority leader bid ahead of the early December caucus elections. “I’m trying to talk to our members, and I think it’s important to reach out to everybody,” he said in the Capitol halls. Flanagan said she had not had “formal conversations” with Van Hollen, but another younger Democrat — Sen. Elissa Slotkin of Michigan — met with him this week as she called for a leadership shakeup. Outside the building, at a gathering of progressive groups charting an agenda for the coming Democratic majorities, Van Hollen was sharply critical of the existing Senate Democratic power structure — and Schumer in particular. “We just saw democracy in America in action — we should bring a little more democracy to the United States Senate,” he said, before later accusing Schumer and the Senate Democratic campaign arm of having “sided with the crypto industry and AIPAC” to oppose more progressive candidates in this year’s primaries. That outspokenness has gotten Van Hollen noticed on the left — and it has been especially striking coming from a son of prominent U.S. diplomats who spent decades dutifully rising through the Democratic Party establishment and chaired both the House and Senate campaign committees. “Van Hollen represents a bridge between the old guard — people who’ve been in office for a long time with a more moderate orientation — and the new generation that is coming into office,” said Joseph Geevarghese, executive director of Our Revolution. His rhetoric and actions have evolved dramatically, however, since Trump returned to office in 2025. The administration’s spending cuts decimated Van Hollen’s constituency — particularly in his political base of Montgomery County — and his posts on the Appropriations and Foreign Relations committees gave him a front-row seat to Trump’s elimination of USAID. Meanwhile, he became an outspoken critic of the White House’s mass deportation agenda and was the first U.S. lawmaker to visit the El Salvador prison where the administration was sending scores of deportees — including a Maryland man, Kilmar Ábrego García, who had been mistakenly deported in contravention of a court order. Van Hollen has also become increasingly critical of the U.S. posture toward Israel, joining early Democratic pushes to restrict arms sales to Benjamin Netanyahu’s government as its war on Gaza after the 2023 Hamas attacks grew increasingly brutal. “He’s been correct,” said Jeff Cohen, founder of RootsAction, a group pushing its members to back Van Hollen over Schumer. “He’s been with the base of the party on most issues: redefining the U.S.-Israel relationship is one. Taxing the wealthy is another, standing up to AI — all of these issues that Schumer is wrong on.” Van Hollen’s approach to the Senate leadership race has evolved in recent days. He downplayed a bid for top leader earlier this year, including saying in a recent interview that it has “not been my focus.” The day after the election, Michigan Sen.-elect Abdul El-Sayed appeared to believe he had passed on a run, calling Van Hollen “my white whale” in response to a question about his ideal Senate leader. But asked about the matter Tuesday as the drumbeat for his candidacy grew, Van Hollen said there should not be a “coronation” for Schumer as he described his ongoing listening tour. “We should not support anybody for leader without a very clear plan and as you know, there are many people who think that a change is required,” he said. A Senate aide who was granted anonymity to describe Van Hollen’s thinking said the senator has been influenced by the scale of his party’s midterm victory and the calls he has heard for change — as well as the public outreach he is getting. The aide said Van Hollen is not coordinating the outside effort to nudge him into challenging Schumer. Senate Democrats still broadly expect Schumer to be reelected as leader, and some are openly warning Van Hollen away from jumping into the race. “I'm going to vote for Schumer. He helped recruit a great class, and I can't imagine why you would vote for someone like Van Hollen with no record of doing anything,” pro-Israel Sen. John Fetterman (D-Pa.) told reporters. Asked about whether Van Hollen will run, Fetterman added, “I dare him to.” Schumer’s backers point to his decades of fundraising experience, deep well of relationships within the caucus and across the party, and his work to unite his colleagues and battle Trump over the past year. And with Democrats poised to pick up as many as nine seats — a once-unthinkable outcome — they are questioning why senators would depose the leader who helped make it happen. "When the manager takes you to the World Series, you give him another contract,” Sen. Ruben Gallego (D-Ariz.) said Tuesday at a joint news conference with Schumer. But those arguments are carrying little water with those who view Schumer as out of touch with the direction of the party. They note that while he supported the incoming freshmen with hundreds of millions of dollars of general-election spending, he opposed some of them during the primary. Van Hollen could be using his flirtations with a bid to influence some end-of-year decisionmaking. He is pushing Congress to cut off Iran war funding as they head toward a Dec. 11 government funding deadline, and he wants a provision mandating cooperation with Israel stripped from the annual defense policy bill. Those stances could help push Schumer and the party into a more confrontational posture, which Van Hollen signaled he wanted in an interview earlier this year. “It’s going to be very important that Democrats let voters know not only what we’re against but what we stand for,” he said. “And I think a lot of voters, you know, think Democrats have been too much finger-in-the-wind. They’ve been too wishy-washy.” Grace Yarrow and Lisa Kashinsky contributed to this report. articles.title: Alina Habba Mildon fired from company that gave her $50 million deal before Trump pardon
articles.summary: Alina Habba Mildon , a former attorney for President Donald Trump , has been terminated from her multi-million-dollar role at Florida-registered Concord Partners following months of intense public scrutiny, according to reports. In a November 4 termination letter obtained by The New York Times , Concord Partners — a firm established by the family of Venezuelan billionaire banker Julio Herrera Velutini — cited a "failure to perform duties" as the reason for releasing  Mildon. A source close to the family told the publication that Mildon’s attention shifted away from her role after she began dating Turkish investor Turhan Mildon earlier this year. The departure follows public criticism from Trump, who denounced the lucrative arrangement after details of the contract were disclosed. "I thought it was terrible," Trump told reporters last month, according to The New York Times . "I told her, and I said, I don’t want her paid.' I thought we had somebody speak to the people that did it, and she used her relationship to do that. And it was far too much." Mediaite also reported Trump saying of the arrangement: "You know, it’s one thing for a person to get paid legal fees or whatever — she’s a lawyer. I thought it was a totally obnoxious and outrageous and it’s not acceptable. Not acceptable, at all." Alina Habba Mildon, a former lawyer for President Donald Trump, has been fired from her multi-million dollar position at Florida-registered Concord Partners following months of heavy media coverage, according to reports (Getty Images) Following media coverage of the contract, Trump told aides and allies that the Herrera family should withhold payments to Mildon, suggesting she make a donation to his future presidential library or another entity. When asked by CBS News about the possibility of donating to the library, Mildon responded via text with "haha" before quickly deleting the message, according to Mediaite . Despite her firing, Mildon will retain an $8 million signing bonus and $6.5 million in payments already received. The original four-year agreement, which began on January 1 when she was brought on as general counsel, was structured to pay her $10 million annually plus additional bonuses. Mildon was serving as a special government employee and senior adviser to the attorney general when she joined Concord Partners. Special government employee status permits individuals to serve the federal government for up to 130 days while retaining outside employment, subject to conflict-of-interest guidelines. The move follows public condemnation from Trump, who called the lucrative arrangement ‘obnoxious’ and urged the Florida firm to stop paying his former lawyer (Getty Images) The hiring occurred shortly after Herrera reached a plea agreement in August 2025 that reduced his federal charges — originally related to an alleged 2022 scheme to bribe the governor of Puerto Rico — down to a single misdemeanor campaign finance violation. Around the same time, Herrera's daughter, Isabela Herrera, donated $3.5 million to a super PAC aligned with Trump. Weeks after Concord Partners hired Mildon, Trump granted Herrera a full and unconditional pardon . Mildon has consistently denied that her employment had any connection to the pardon. "Any insinuation that my employment — all of which has been vetted and disclosed to the D.O.J. — had anything to do with securing a pardon is false," Mildon said in a statement previously reported by The New York Times . A person close to Mildon said she intends to pursue legal action over the termination. Despite her abrupt departure, Mildon will keep $14.5 million in payments and signing bonuses from the four-year agreement (Getty Images) The termination comes after a series of setbacks for the couple following their September wedding in New York. The New York Times reported recently that Turhan Mildon gave misleading or exaggerated accounts of his age, past marriages, foreign contacts and business operations. Additionally, Turhan Mildon remains central to a White House inquiry initiated after Mildon accused former Trump administration official Richard Grenell of skimming funds from a donation made by her husband. Upon investigating the claims at Trump's directive, White House officials determined that the $17.6 million in question originated from a government account in the Democratic Republic of Congo — where Turhan Mildon holds business contracts — rather than from Turhan Mildon's personal funds, as reported by The New York Times . articles.title: 芯片制造商“严阵以待”，反思产业链绑定太深，“英伟达事件”让韩国AI产业界揪心
articles.summary: “在英伟达启动黄仁勋调查之际，韩国芯片制造商‘严阵以待’准备应对冲击。”韩国《中央日报》10日报道称，英伟达首席执行官黄仁勋的个人婚外情事件给韩国半导体行业带来了“不确定性的涟漪”。英伟达领导层可能产生的变动或会对韩国芯片制造商和更广泛的人工智能（AI）产业生态产生深远影响。近年来，英伟达与韩企的合作已从内存芯片全面拓展至AI数据中心、机器人及自动驾驶等关键领域。尽管目前尚未出现项目停摆或供货中断，但韩媒担忧，若调查长期化拖累英伟达的投资与经营决策，与其深度绑定的韩国企业恐遭连锁冲击。这场突发风波，也让韩国AI产业长期高度依赖单一巨头的深层隐患浮出水面。 韩国半导体市场再添不确定性 据韩联社报道，美国国会已要求黄仁勋于18日出席闭门简报会说明情况。连日来事件持续引发股市震荡。英伟达股价9日下跌4.27%，10日再跌5.47%，连续两日大幅下挫，市值一度蒸发约4000亿美元。韩国7只名称中包含英伟达的交易型开放式指数基金在9日全线下跌，最大跌幅近2%。韩国News1通讯社称，这场风波令刚经历暴跌的韩国半导体股再蒙阴影。此前因市场担忧美国中期选举后可能加码AI监管，三星电子和SK海力士连续4日大跌。虽然11日韩国股市半导体企业出现反弹，但近日连遭外资卖出后市场信心依然脆弱。 韩国证券业更担心，“英伟达事件”可能引发新一轮半导体出口管制。韩华投资证券分析师朴世妍称，真正影响韩国供应链的并非高管私人生活，而是美国是否出台新的出口限制，以及英伟达的客户和合同是否发生变化。三星电子和SK海力士均在中国设有生产基地，其设备进口和生产线升级本就受到美国出口许可政策制约。一旦美方进一步收紧相关规定，韩企经营负担恐进一步加重。 《韩民族日报》称，英伟达长期依赖黄仁勋个人领导力。一旦黄仁勋离任，英伟达的重大经营决策及与韩国企业的长期合作都可能受到影响。英伟达是SK海力士重要客户，三星电子也正向其供应最新一代高带宽内存（HBM），并洽谈后续产品供应。《中央日报》报道称，SK海力士今年6月与英伟达签署多年技术协议，共同开发下一代AI芯片所需的内存。韩国财经媒体EBN表示，HBM需要针对客户的AI芯片进行定制开发和验证，已生产的产品难以迅速转供其他企业。一旦英伟达调整采购或产品开发计划，韩企的生产安排也可能被打乱。 据韩国《首尔经济》分析，“英伟达事件”可能为超威半导体、谷歌等竞争对手扩大市场份额提供机会，韩国存储芯片企业也将面临新的经营压力。三星电子正积极拓展超威半导体、博通等客户，而高度依赖英伟达内存芯片订单的SK海力士则面临营收受损风险。韩国NH投资证券研究员柳永浩认为，调查长期化可能拖慢英伟达投资决策，甚至延误产品出货和新产品上市，波及韩国整个半导体产业。 AI基础设施建设受牵连 英伟达的经营风险不仅牵动韩国半导体订单，也可能波及AI基础设施建设及其他合作项目。据韩联社报道，英伟达6日完成对韩国互联网巨头NAVER的投资并获得4.13%的股份，成为其第三大股东。双方正与其他合作伙伴推进规模达90亿美元的AI计算基础设施项目。一旦英伟达调整芯片交付时间或供货数量，NAVER数据中心恐面临启用延期、算力供应缩水等风险。英伟达在韩活动也出现变动。原定出席首尔“AI Day Seoul”的英伟达高级总监黄敏珊（黄仁勋长女）突然取消访韩，其与韩国高层官员的会面随之取消。 不过，英伟达仍在首尔活动期间公布多项与韩国合作的进展，三星电子、SK海力士、现代汽车及LG电子也在半导体制造、机器人开发等领域使用英伟达技术。韩联社称，这些项目尚未出现中断迹象。韩国总统李在明此前表示，希望将韩国建设为全球人工智能领域的领先力量。2025年，英伟达与韩国政府和4家韩企达成约26万块图形处理器（GPU）的供应合同以支持韩国的AI基础设施建设。韩国政府目前判断既定GPU供应不会立即受到冲击。 “对韩国公司来说，后果是毁灭性的” 《韩民族日报》评论称，此次事件暴露出韩国AI产业对英伟达的高度依赖。去年10月，韩国政府和主要企业公布的合作计划显示，从半导体制造业到云计算，英伟达已深度嵌入韩国AI产业链，令单家企业的经营风险可能向韩国多个行业蔓延。 韩国对外经济政策研究院研究员郑亨坤向韩国《中央日报》表示，韩国半导体产业真正的风险是供应链日益依赖单一企业及其生态系统。韩媒称，韩国政府和企业应检查GPU采购合同及供货进度，加快推动合作伙伴多元化，摆脱对英伟达的过度依赖。“如果英伟达的信誉下降，半导体市场因此萎缩，那么对韩国公司来说，后果可能是毁灭性的。”祥明大学系统半导体工程系教授李钟焕这样表示。 本文来源： 环球时报 风险提示及免责条款 articles.title: 今日开会决定“黄仁勋是否下台”！英伟达董事会已开始遴选新CEO，考虑任命过渡CEO
articles.summary: 英伟达正面临一场可能重塑这家全球最高市值人工智能芯片制造商领导架构的严峻危机。因首席执行官黄仁勋卷入多起婚外情丑闻，公司董事会目前正积极寻找潜在的继任者，以应对可能出现的权力真空。 据彭博和《华尔街日报》报道， 英伟达董事会于周三召开内部会议以决定黄仁勋的去留，并已与外部机构合作遴选新任CEO候选人，其中包括考虑任命一位过渡时期首席执行官。 此前，《纽约时报》最新披露了黄仁勋与一名直接下属存在不正当关系，这一消息进一步加剧了早前关于其与一名中国女性有染的严重指控。 继任不确定性迅速引发了金融市场的剧烈反应。在周三的盘后交易中，英伟达股价重挫9%，不仅单日抹去巨额市值，还引发了广泛的抛售情绪，拖累Intel、Dell Technologies等其他人工智能概念股同步下挫。 随着英伟达即将在下周发布季度财报，这一连串突发事件迫使投资者必须直面史无前例的“关键人物风险”。华尔街正密切评估，如果这位人工智能基础设施的核心架构师被迫离职，将对整个AI行业的资金链、客户信心与发展前景造成何种程度的直接冲击。 独立调查与董事会面临大考 据路透报道，英伟达董事会已于周日启动内部调查，以应对新闻报道中提及的国家安全隐患。然而，该公司的治理结构正受到外界的严格审视。英伟达的11名董事中并未设立董事会主席，且多位独立董事（如Mark Stevens）自上世纪90年代起便开始任职，人员结构高度固化。 机构股东服务公司（ISS）美国研究主管Marc Goldstein指出，尽管华尔街通常会给予硅谷魅力型创始人一定的宽容度，但由于黄仁勋自身的判断力已受到质疑，董事会必须聘请独立的法律顾问以增强调查的公信力。他建议董事会考虑让长期任职的董事回避调查，以防范股东未来发起法律挑战。前美国司法部官员Gil Soffer则强调，如果调查证实黄仁勋隐瞒了相关关系并存在不当行为，那么将其罢免是适当的决定。 华尔街重估“关键人物风险” 市场分析师对英伟达可能面临的领导层动荡表达了普遍担忧。Karobaar Capital首席投资官Haris Khurshid指出，这已不再是单一的个人丑闻，而是演变为严重的治理和关键人物风险，投资者正开始重新定价整个AI赛道的情绪。Integrity Asset Management投资组合经理Joe Gilbert明确表示，这对英伟达及整个AI生态系统是“毫无疑问的负面影响”，因为新任者几乎不可能复制黄仁勋的战略眼光。 Jonestrading首席市场策略师Michael O’Rourke指出，英伟达此前预测今年销售额将增长70%，在激进的销售策略和供应商融资模式下，继任者可能需要花一整年时间来“灭火和清理烂摊子”。Miller Tabak + Co首席市场策略师Matt Maley则警告，英伟达作为AI行业的重要融资方，其高层动荡可能会导致整个行业缩减支出。Zacks Investment Management的Brian Mulberry认为，即便黄仁勋卸任CEO，他仍有可能作为战略顾问或董事会成员保留一定的职能。 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。

articles.title: 11月12日会员早报：Anthropic IPO获数倍超额认购 英伟达董事会据报准备罢免黄仁勋
articles.summary: 1、【Anthropic IPO获数倍超额认购】据彭博社11月11日援引知情人士报道，Claude开发商Anthropic的IPO已获得数倍于发行股数的认购，需求主要来自基石投资者级别的大额认购意向。根据监管文件，按发行价区间上限计算，Anthropic及其联合创始人通过IPO和同步私募合计最多可募资904亿美元，这一数字低于部分投资者此前的预期。若顺利完成，其规模将超过SpaceX今年6月的IPO，成为史上最大的上市融资。 2、【英伟达董事会据报准备罢免黄仁勋】据《华尔街日报》美东时间11月11日援引知情人士报道，英伟达董事会正准备罢免联合创始人兼首席执行官黄仁勋，起因是他的两段婚外情相继曝光。消息传出后，英伟达股价盘后跌幅一度扩大至9%。截至发稿，董事会没有公布任何决定，英伟达也没有确认将撤换黄仁勋。 3、【AI交易重燃纳指100大涨2.28%】11月11日周三，一周前刚遭重挫的AI板块强势反攻。纳斯达克100指数收涨2.28%，报28374.25点，盘中升至11月4日以来最高水平，并录得一周来首次站上200日均线的收盘。标普500指数涨1.31%，距历史高点不足2.6%。道指涨0.49%，纳斯达克综合指数涨1.60%，报25466.19点。CoreWeave乐观的业绩展望、Anthropic IPO的强劲需求，以及OpenAI营收的大幅增长，共同重燃了市场对AI的乐观情绪。 4、【伦铝挤仓创三十余年之最：现货升水一度飙至每吨147美元】伦敦金属交易所（LME）铝市场正经历数十年来最严峻的供应挤压，近月流动性急剧收紧。周三（11月11日），LME铝现货价格盘中一度比三个月期货高出每吨147美元，为逾三十年来最高。据彭博稍晚报道，这一升水盘中最高触及151美元，为逾30年数据记录之最；而就在10月中旬，该价差还处于贴水状态。 5、【万斯考虑与伊朗安全首脑雷扎伊面谈，谋求结束美伊战争】据《华尔街日报》11日援引美国和中东官员报道，美国副总统万斯正考虑与伊朗一名高级安全官员举行面对面会谈，为华盛顿寻找结束对伊战争的出路。相关讨论仍处于早期阶段，尚未确定日期。会谈对象是伊朗最高国家安全委员会秘书穆赫辛·雷扎伊，此举等于让万斯以美方首席谈判代表的身份直接对接德黑兰。知情人士称，会谈如果成行，地点可能在多哈。

articles.title: CoreWeave拟发行至少40亿美元投资级贷款，盘后下挫近6%
articles.summary: AI算力供应商CoreWeave正寻求通过投资级贷款再度大规模融资。 11月11日，据彭博社援引知情人士透露， 摩根士丹利与三菱日联金融集团（MUFG）正主导该笔至少40亿美元的潜在融资，计划分阶段向投资者进行银团推介，最快可能于下周启动，但方案尚未最终确定。 CoreWeave周二发布财报，将全年营收指引上调至130亿至133亿美元，高于此前预期区间，也超出华尔街平均预期的129亿美元。公司股价周三大幅上涨，债券价格亦随之走高。 消息公布后，CoreWeave盘后下挫近6%。 这笔融资将为其以芯片及相关合同作为抵押、借助投资级评级压低融资成本的运作模式提供又一次市场检验。CoreWeave今年3月已通过类似架构完成一笔85亿美元的投资级融资，新融资的定价则有望进一步收紧。 以芯片合同为抵押，锁定投资级利率 尽管CoreWeave在信用评级上仍属垃圾级，但该公司通过将英伟达芯片及客户合同作为底层抵押资产，成功在部分融资安排上获得投资级评级，从而显著降低融资成本。 据报道，这一结构预计将沿用至此次新融资中。根据CoreWeave周二财报电话会议上披露的信息， 新融资的发行收益率初步讨论区间约为7%至7.5%，大约是其现有垃圾级债券当前交易收益率的一半。 今年3月完成的85亿美元投资级融资由Meta的客户合同背书，分为两个部分：一笔浮动利率档，利差为有担保隔夜融资利率（SOFR）上加225个基点；另一笔固定利率档，融资利率约为5.9%。 高负债扩张模式受审视，AI基础设施投资回报存疑 CoreWeave为Meta等大型科技平台提供算力服务，其业务处于AI基础设施投资能否产生足够回报这一市场争议的核心。 该公司长期依赖高收益债券市场为大规模基础设施建设提供资金，高负债模式持续引发投资者关注。 此番大幅上调的营收指引，以及高管在财报会议上明确表达的再融资意愿，在一定程度上缓解了外界对其偿债能力的疑虑，推动股债双涨。 据报道，CoreWeave方面和摩根士丹利对此融资计划拒绝置评，MUFG未回应置评请求。融资方案能否顺利落地，仍将取决于市场对该公司债务的实际承接意愿。 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。

articles.title: 政策工具优化迭代，稳市机制加快完善
articles.summary: 金融管理部门部署推动支持资本市场两项工具调整优化、加力实施，一周多来，超过10家券商已在第三批证券、基金、保险公司互换便利项下买入股票，银行机构两日即申报股票回购增持再贷款额度超过2000亿元，上市公司密集抛出回购增持方案，政策红利正快速转化为真金白银的稳市力量。 11月6日召开的国务院常务会议提出“完善资本市场稳市机制”。业内专家认为，我国稳市工具体系日益完善，稳市机制从“应急托底”逐渐转向“长效制度安排”，市场抵御外部冲击、平滑波动的韧性有望增强。 稳市政策高效落地 金融管理部门11月2日召开座谈会，推动支持资本市场两项货币政策工具调整优化、加力实施，并随后落地多个务实举措。 “金融管理部门出台的一系列稳市场稳预期举措，重在用好用足现有稳市工具，政策落地节奏较快。”中国银河证券首席经济学家、研究院院长章俊对上海证券报记者表示。 从实施成效看，章俊认为，互换便利资金快速到位，上市公司使用回购增持贷款的相关公告密集发布。相关政策部署有助于增强机构逆势配置能力、降低回购增持融资成本、完善上市公司回购机制，从而提升资本市场韧性。 “本次政策优化及落地执行，展现出极高的统筹效率与微观穿透力。金融机构、上市公司的积极响应，形成了政策引导与龙头示范的正向循环。”南开大学金融发展研究院院长田利辉对记者表示。 第三批证券、基金、保险公司互换便利启动后，中金公司、中信证券、中信建投证券等超过10家券商已完成首批股票买入操作。 章俊表示：短期内，互换便利操作可以有效缓解机构的流动性压力、抑制被动抛压；中长期看，有助于撬动更大规模的资金流入A股，为市场带来增量买盘，增厚机构长期配置能力。 股票回购增持再贷款政策迎来加码：利率下调0.25个百分点至1%，由阶段性安排转为长期制度性安排。 政策激励之下，上市公司回购增持动作密集。洛阳钼业等公司发布回购方案，并明确已取得金融机构股票回购专项贷款承诺函。 “股票回购增持再贷款加力实施，从三方面夯实市场韧性。”北京大学光华管理学院院长、北京大学博雅特聘教授田轩对记者表示：逆周期调节常态化，使市场不再依赖临时性政策托底，而是有了制度化的资金供给通道；上市公司和主要股东获得低成本资金支持后，回购增持的意愿和执行力显著增强，市值管理从被动应对转向主动作为，由此增强市场相关主体的内生稳定力量；当非理性下跌出现时，多个主体可以同时发力，缩短市场调整的时间和深度。 展望长远，田利辉认为，常态化的低成本回购渠道与逆周期调节机制，将增强上市公司与机构投资者跨越周期的定力，使资本市场在面对外部扰动与输入性风险时，具备更强的自我修复能力。 完善资本市场稳市机制 11月6日召开的国务院常务会议首次提出“完善资本市场稳市机制”，同时要求增强股市内在稳定性，促进资本市场平稳健康发展。 在业内专家看来，这一表述凸显资本市场稳定在宏观经济大局中的定位，稳市机制建设将成为跨部门协同推进的制度安排。 “‘稳’从来不是稳点位，而是稳机制，让市场在自我修复中保持价格发现功能、资源配置功能和预期引导功能。”田轩表示，“完善资本市场稳市机制”的核心意义，是把稳市从临时性、应急式干预，升级为可预期、可持续的制度性安排，厘清“何种条件下启动，谁来执行，用什么工具，如何有序退出”等关键问题，以规则代替相机决策，让市场参与主体形成稳定预期。 “完备的稳市机制应涵盖完善的资金支持体系、坚实的资产端价值根基和清晰的运行规则。”章俊表示：要持续提升上市公司质量，完善分红、回购注销制度，推动投融资综合改革，增强市场内在稳定性；要明确稳市工具使用的触发条件、投资边界与退出机制，加强跨部门协调与政策沟通，稳定市场政策预期。 稳市工具体系日益完善 近年来，我国持续推动资本市场稳市机制建设。2024年，金融管理部门创设支持资本市场两项工具；2025年起，支持中央汇金公司发挥类平准基金作用，拓宽中长期资金来源、渠道和入市方式，巩固完善资本市场稳市机制…… 章俊认为，我国稳市工具体系日益完善，稳市机制从“应急托底”逐渐转向“长效制度安排”，市场抵御外部冲击、平滑波动的韧性增强。 章俊还表示，近年来，央行流动性支持与资本市场的衔接更加紧密，中央汇金公司持续发挥类平准基金功能，资本市场内生稳定制度也不断健全。 “我国在资本市场稳市机制建设上，已经基本实现‘从工具到机制、从应急式到常态化安排’的转变。”田轩表示。 田轩认为，我国资本市场已初步形成“央行提供流动性—中央汇金公司逆周期调节—上市公司自主护盘”的三层稳市架构。 田轩表示，其中：央行通过两项货币政策工具提供流动性支持和成本优势；中央汇金公司以类平准基金角色承担逆周期调节职能；上市公司及股东通过回购增持在微观层面稳定股价预期。三层架构各有分工、相互衔接，一套完整的规则闭环正在持续完善。 本文来源： 上海证券报 风险提示及免责条款 articles.title: 巴西提出最高108亿美元财政整顿方案，拟削减税收优惠、收紧支出
articles.summary: 巴西政府提出一揽子财政整顿措施，预计明年可改善公共财政最多600亿雷亚尔（约108亿美元），以回应市场对该国债务可持续性的持续担忧。 据路透社报道， 巴西规划部长Bruno Moretti周三在国会听证会上表示，该方案涵盖削减税收减免、限制税收抵扣使用以及约束公共部门薪酬等多项举措，同时寻求授权政府在必要时实施更大力度的支出冻结。 Moretti称， 政府"绝对确信"明年能够实现占GDP 0.1%的实际基本盈余。 该消息公布之际，市场仍承压于对巴西财政前景的隐忧。自总统路易斯·伊纳西奥·卢拉·达席尔瓦（Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva）10月25日赢得连任以来，巴西雷亚尔持续走低，长期利率攀升，股市承压。 然而，方案在卢拉所属劳工党内部已遭遇明显抵触，立法前景存在不确定性。 方案核心：多重工具压缩财政缺口 根据Moretti的介绍， 本次财政方案的核心是在现行财政框架的2.5%实际支出增长上限基础上进一步收紧，将实际支出增长限制在2%。 若有需要，政府可启动机制，限制企业以税收抵免冲抵应缴税款，释放约500亿雷亚尔的财政缓冲空间；在此基础上，对特定支出设定上限，将整体财政影响推升至600亿雷亚尔。 方案还提议对各类税收减免进行全面削减，并将意外石油收入排除在净经常性收入的计算口径之外。 Moretti解释，由于巴西财政规则将医疗最低支出与净经常性收入挂钩，这一调整将有效限制强制性医疗支出的增长。此外，方案亦包含约束公共部门薪酬过度增长的相关措施。 Moretti强调，上述措施旨在为政府提供更多工具以管控支出、审查税收优惠政策，并非削减民众权利或社会福利，健全的公共财政恰恰是保障社会福利可持续兑现的前提。 财政目标：守住盈余承诺，兼顾社会支出 Moretti表示， 该方案的首要目标是确保政府实现明年相当于GDP 0.5%基本盈余的官方目标 ，同时为卢拉竞选期间承诺的社会支出留出空间，包括扩大"家庭补贴"（Bolsa Família）现金援助项目的覆盖范围。 根据巴西现行财政框架，政府可将约650亿雷亚尔的特定支出排除在2027年目标测算之外，目标本身亦设有GDP的0.25个百分点的上下容忍区间。 今年8月，政府已向国会提交了2027年预算草案，其中纳入了0.1%的实际基本盈余预测，该草案目前仍待国会审批。 党内阻力：执政联盟内部出现裂痕信号 尽管方案由劳工党资深成员Jaques Wagner正式提交参议院，但党内反弹已在当日浮现。 劳工党议员Lindbergh Farias公开警告， 若在缺乏广泛讨论的情况下强行推进该方案，可能导致执政联盟出现裂痕。 "这不是走过场，"Farias表示，"这里的人们是真心希望卢拉政府成功的。" 这一表态折射出卢拉政府在推进财政整顿时面临的内部张力——既需向市场传递约束支出、稳定债务的信号，又须维系左翼执政联盟对社会政策承诺的政治共识。方案最终能否顺利通过国会，仍面临相当变数。 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。

articles.title: 最低三折卖Token！大模型厂商，首次卷向“双11”
articles.summary: 11月11日，天猫商城的天猫AI空间站显示，智谱、MiniMax、千问AI、Qoder等大模型厂商，相继推出五折甚至三折的Token（词元）订阅套餐。 这是大模型厂商首次集体参与“双11”网络促销活动，也是其加速向C端（消费端）商业化进程的重要营销事件。 在“双11”网络促销活动开始前夕，部分头部大模型厂商“踩点”展现产品力。 11月10日23时，MiniMax发布图像生成模型MiniMax H3-Image，并开放模型权重，出图速度最高可达主流工具的5倍，定价低至50%。 大模型厂商C端商业化加速 自9月初开始，多家头部大模型厂商相继入驻电商平台卖Token。 目前，用户在电商平台搜索“Token”，即可进入聚合选购页面，充值入口与话费、流量、生活缴费相同，购买流程也与常规数字充值商品一致。 区别在于，多家大模型厂商在“双11”网络促销活动期间，推出了优惠力度更大的Token订阅套餐。 天猫AI空间站显示，MiniMax月卡全场五折、千问Token Plan两款月卡五折起、智谱周卡五折起、Qoder专业版月卡低至三折，并且都标注“双11专享”。 对于大模型厂商来说，借助“双11”网络促销活动的知名度，可以低成本触达此前没有覆盖的散客群体，包括一人公司、小团队、普通办公人群等。 公开资料显示，“双11”网络促销活动已成为中国电商行业的年度盛事，并且主阵地在天猫商城、京东商城等电商平台。 在入驻电商平台售卖Token订阅套餐之前，各家大模型厂商已经建立了官网、开放平台、App内购等渠道，可以直接对外售卖算力，但受众较窄。 同时，大模型厂商依赖政企项目，会导致收入结构波动较大，而C端订阅服务是寻找稳定现金流的新方向。 “双11”前夕推出重要新模型 有别于其他头部大模型厂商，MiniMax借力“双11”网络促销活动的动作，还包括在11月10日23时发布MiniMax H3-Image并开放权重。 MiniMax H3-Image是一款衍生自MiniMax H3的图像生成模型，具备文本生成图像、图像参考和图像编辑能力。 MiniMax H3-Image能在10秒内生成一张4096 ×4096像素、约16MP（4K）的高分辨率图像，同时呈现丰富、真实的细节，并具备优秀的指令遵循和多参考图理解能力。 近期，MiniMax CEO闫俊杰表示，下一阶段，MiniMax及大模型行业的增长来源仍是模型能力的提升。 在闫俊杰看来，更强的模型会带来更多新客户和任务，更好的推理效率会让客户以可接受的成本扩大使用。 MiniMax H3-Image将开源图像模型的能力上限提升到新维度，即能否准确理解复杂的创作要求，以及能否把这些要求转化为有美感、有真实感的画面。 MiniMax H3-Image开源首日，MiniMax与华为昇腾、平头哥、昆仑芯、摩尔线程、壁仞、海光、沐曦、天数、NVIDIA、AMD、英特尔等全球芯片企业与多家主流推理和云服务平台推进Day 0接入工作。 据悉，为了让更多用户体验高质量图像生成能力，MiniMax将在MiniMax H3-Image发布首周，针对16MP及以上规格的生成请求，提供官方价格的五折优惠。 图：MiniMax H3-Image单张生成费用参考 本文来源： 中国基金报 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。
